checks: The accepted all-normal value uses the same area-one product and parameters t,L. Its rational partition covers the entire closed rectangle, the SOS term is positive on the open t strip, and D is positive there.

Replayed the exact verifier for 35 cells, 42 triangles and 420 Bernstein coefficients. Independently recalculated the additional minima and counts, obtaining 229/125 in 42 largest-coefficient occurrences, 229/125 in 92 open-strip vertex occurrences, and 12949/16000 in 115 open-strip edge-midpoint occurrences.

Nonnegative Bernstein coefficients with a positive coefficient give interior positivity. On a relative interior of an edge all its restricted basis weights are positive, so the edge midpoint tests give positivity on the whole open edge. Checked vertices and the SOS cell cover the remaining cases.

The endpoint minima isolate t=−1,L=2/11. A negative L can only match its positive counterpart at this pair, where its unpaired tail is strictly larger. Pure-base caps and large tilts are strictly above 112/33.

Through-center equality translates to the three stated barycentric thresholds. Tightening a strictly containing cap gives strict own-fiber gain in the original cap, while moving the canonical threshold at a noncentroid middle point strictly decreases its own mass. The nonmiddle bound 22/9 applies to arbitrary marks on those bases. The statement is the complete-menu extension in source d4522420ea2ebef1 §§1–4 and Appendix A.
